claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son Alex, who is 16 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 16, there are some additional criteria to consider. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or undertaking an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Alex being in college doing A-levels counts as approved education.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Leeds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to ask about Alex's work and benefit situation:

**Does Alex do any paid work? And if so, is it for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, that's very helpful. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Does Alex receive any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not actually sure about that - I don't think so, but I'm not certain whether he receives anything in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your honesty about not being certain. Let me ask this slightly differently to help clarify:

**To the best of your knowledge, has Alex applied for or been awarded any benefits such as Universal Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, or any other benefits that would be paid directly to him?** 

(If he hasn't applied for anything and hasn't received any correspondence about benefits in his name, it's likely he doesn't receive any benefits in his own right.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, as far as I know he hasn't applied for anything like that, and I haven't seen any letters or correspondence about benefits in his name. So I don't believe he's receiving anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Let me consider the key facts:
- Alex is 16 years old
- He lives at home with you in the UK (Leeds)
- He is in approved education (doing A-levels at college)
- He does not do paid work for 24 hours or more per week
- He does not receive benefits in his own right

Based on the rules for Child Benefit, you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16. However, you'll still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 16, in approved education (A-levels), not working 24+ hours per week, and not receiving benefits in his own right, you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility criteria:

✓ Alex is 16 and lives with you in the UK  
✓ He's in approved education (A-levels at college)  
✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week  
✓ He's not receiving benefits in his own right  

Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 as long as they remain in approved education or training, which Alex is.

**Please note:** You should inform HMRC if Alex's circumstances change - for example, if he:
- Leaves education or training
- Starts working 24 hours or more per week
- Starts receiving benefits in his own right

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can apply through HMRC. If you're already receiving it, it should continue as long as Alex remains in education.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
